title: Forecasting and Planning
answer: Rolling forecasts, external signals in revenue models, variance explanation, capital spending and zero-based budgeting.

sections.body: Forecasting and planning covers how organizations use machine learning and statistical models to predict future financial outcomes and allocate resources. In practice, artificial intelligence is being used to update rolling forecasts with recent transaction data, to pull external signals like commodity prices or shipping rates into revenue models, and to flag which line items in a budget explain a variance. It is also used to score proposed capital projects and to rebuild budgets from zero by grouping similar cost drivers. These are not autonomous systems; they are tools that produce candidate numbers and explanations for finance teams to review.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The work is uneven. Rolling forecasts and variance explanation are the most mature, because they rely on internal data that is already structured and available. External signals in revenue models remain harder, since data quality and timing vary widely across sources. Capital spending decisions and zero-based budgeting are less automated, because they involve judgment about strategy, risk, and organizational priorities that models cannot yet capture. Honest limits include unstable relationships during shocks, missing data, and the need for human review of every material forecast.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages under this section move from routine forecasting to more judgment-heavy planning. Rolling Forecasts explains how models update near-term projections as new data arrives. External Signals in Revenue Models covers the use of outside data like freight costs or weather in revenue estimates. Variance Analysis and Explanation shows how systems compare actuals to forecasts and generate plain language reasons for differences. Capital Spending Decisions and Zero-Based Budgeting then turn to longer horizon and structural choices, where artificial intelligence supports rather than replaces the finance team.
